**Changing the target changes what errors are expensive.** A tree trained with raw squared error treats a miss of 100 as equally costly whether the true value is 200 or 20,000. Squared error on log targets instead emphasizes multiplicative differences. Doubling and halving values become comparable changes in log space. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/ensemble.html)

Consider one leaf containing targets 1 and 9. Its raw-MSE optimum is the arithmetic mean, 5. In log space, the optimum is $(\log1+\log9)/2=\log3$, whose exponent is 3: the geometric mean. These are different predictions for the same data.

**Splits change too.** The tree chooses partitions by reduction in its loss. A split that isolates one huge raw target may be highly valuable under raw MSE and less dominant after logarithmic compression. Thus feature-order invariance provides no invariance guarantee for target transformation.

Exponentiating an estimated conditional mean of log(Y) generally does not produce the conditional arithmetic mean of Y. If mean forecasting is required, a suitable retransformation or distributional correction may be needed and must be validated. Logs also require positive values or a justified alternative transformation. Choose the target scale according to the application's error costs rather than merely making a distribution look more symmetric.

**Technical details and references.**

MSE on raw targets selects arithmetic means in leaves and rewards splits according to raw squared-error reduction. MSE on log targets instead selects mean log values and uses a different error geometry, so both leaf values and split choices can change. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/ensemble.html)

$$\exp\left(\frac1n\sum_i\log y_i\right)$$

is the geometric mean, not generally the conditional arithmetic mean of $Y$. Exponentiating a predicted mean log target therefore introduces retransformation bias for mean forecasting; a distributional correction or smearing estimate may be appropriate. Log transforms require positive targets or an explicitly justified alternative. They emphasize relative errors and downweight large absolute values, which may or may not match the application's costs.
